gaps.sentence: She wishes she ___ the job offer when it came.
gaps.explanation: Regret about a past decision takes the past perfect: had accepted.

gaps.sentence: Unless something urgent ___, I will be at my desk all morning.
gaps.hint: unless introduces the exception, present simple
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' introduces the exception to the plan and takes the present simple: comes up.

gaps.sentence: If we had left earlier, we ___ the ferry.
gaps.hint: unreal past, would have plus participle
gaps.explanation: Third conditionals take 'would have' plus the past participle in the result clause: would have caught.

gaps.sentence: In case of fire, ___ the nearest exit.
gaps.hint: in case of plus an emergency instruction
gaps.explanation: 'In case of' plus a noun introduces an emergency instruction with the imperative: use.

gaps.sentence: If the pain ___, stop taking the tablets and call your doctor.
gaps.hint: medical instruction with present after if
gaps.explanation: Conditional instructions use the present simple in the if-clause: gets worse.

gaps.sentence: ___ harder, she would have passed the exam.
gaps.hint: inversion replaces if in formal English
gaps.explanation: Formal English can drop 'if' and invert: Had she studied harder, she would have passed.

gaps.sentence: Unless you ___ the form by Friday, your application will not be considered.
gaps.hint: unless means if not, present simple
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if not' and, like if, takes the present simple: submit.

gaps.sentence: As long as you ___ the rules, you will have no problems here.
gaps.hint: as long as states the condition
gaps.explanation: 'As long as' introduces the condition and takes the present simple: follow.
